thread:
maya: Quick sync — product wants per-customer isolation views to spot noisy neighbors + quota overruns. What runtime/infra signals do you need to render useful dashboards in Console?

liam: @eng-runtime +1. Minimal set from runtime: org_id (hashed), model, route, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_size, gpu_id, cache_hit. Send as metrics + occasional full event for traces.

anika: For the UI we need 95/99 pctl latency, request rate, error rate, and a noisy-neighbor score that weights CPU/GPU contention + cache_miss rate. Also want per-tenant quota burn rate.

james: @data-platform can we handle the cardinality? per-org+model+route could explode. Proposal: roll 1) aggregated counters per-minute for all tenants, 2) high-cardinality samples for tenants over a threshold, 3) hashed org ids for team-level view, and clear access controls.

liam: Agreed. Implementation plan from runtime: emit low-cardinality metrics:
```
metric: redwood.requests.count { tags: [model, route, region] }
metric: redwood.latency.p50/p95/p99 { tags: [model, route] }
metric: redwood.tokens.total { tags: [model] }
event: redwood.request.trace -> full payload only when sample=true
```
Plus a small per-request header: `x-org-hash` and `x-tenant-quota-usage` (int).

anika: UX constraints: Console must allow per-org drilldown only if customer granted permission (enterprise). For non-enterprise, show anonymized rankings and allow search by hashed id. Need an RBAC flag to toggle per-tenant panels.

oliver: For noisy neighbor detection, runtime should emit `gpu_util_percent` and `kv_cache_hit_rate` per-node. Aggregator can compute a rolling z-score across tenants on the same worker. If z-score > 3 trigger an alert.

james: Data platform: we can compute z-scores in the metrics pipeline but need an identifier for worker/pool. Add `worker_pool_id` tag. Also prefer delta metrics rather than raw counters to save storage.

liam: Small internal API debate: do we use metrics tags or a single telemetry JSON blob per request? I vote metrics+occasional event. Easier for SLOs and dashboards.

maya: Product note: need a rollout UX — default to aggregated tenant metrics, enable per-tenant only for ent accounts. Can we get a mockup in 2 weeks?

anika: I'll draft the mockups. For the API schema, recommend the following minimal telemetry shape:
```
{
  "org_hash": "sha256(...)",
  "model": "gptx-8k",
  "route": "chat",
  "latency_ms": 210,
  "tokens_in": 32,
  "tokens_out": 128,
  "cache_hit": true,
  "worker_pool_id": "pool-12",
  "sampled": false
}
```
Only `sampled=true` events include stack traces / full prompts.

oliver: Security check — storing `org_hash` is fine, but don't log anything that could reconstruct PII. Add a privacy vetting step before we wire events into long-term storage.

james: Questions for infra: retention tiers? We should keep per-tenant aggregated metrics for 90 days, sampled full events for 30 days, and raw traces for 7 days.

liam: Runtime work items:
- instrument `gpu_util_percent`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`, `batch_size_distribution` (ETA 3w)
- emit per-minute aggregates + sampled request events (ETA 4w)

anika: Console work items:
- initial mockups (2w)
- per-tenant toggle + RBAC (3w)

maya: Owners: runtime = liam, data = james, console = anika. Privacy review = oliver. Delivery target: alpha internal preview in 5 weeks.

data-pipeline-bot: ingestion-pipeline: alert created -> high-cardinality-policy missing for `worker_pool_id`, assigned to @james.

liam: One more: routing policy tie-in — want a flag so Console can trigger automatic fallback to lower-cost model when a tenant exceeds a cost threshold. That requires a control API; will open an RFC.

maya: Perfect. Let's sync on Monday 10am. Thanks all :thumbsup:
